children: TRYING TO Push artificial intelligence Beyond Chatbots... Nikhil Patwardhan & Tanishka Dubey Mumbai: Indian fintech companies are taking artificial intelligence (AI) beyond chatbots, but any initiative allowing software to spend customers' money is in pilot mode, fintech executives said. Most AI deployments remain in fraud detection, customer service and controlled workflows, they told ET on the sidelines of Global Fintech Fest (GFF) here last week.

The Unified Payments Interface (UPI) processed 24.51 billion transactions worth 29.82 lakh crore in August, according to data from the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI). Executives said agentic commerce could sit above these rails, but would require verifiable customer mandates, links across banks and merchants, spending limits and audit trails for errors or disputes.

PhonePe cofounder and chief technology officer Rahul Chari said the payment app uses AI for 80% of trust and safety investigations, with final human verification, and has automated 95% of customer service. PhonePe supports more than 10 billion monthly transactions with fewer than 500 customer-service staff. Chari said AI could improve search, insurance and investments but not materially change core payments. "Agentic commerce is still pretty nascent.

We've not seen much more than proofs of concept," he told ET. Production inside, pilots outside Fintech executives said AI is easier to deploy in company-controlled tasks than when initiating a transaction for a customer. At Flipkart-backed Super.money, chief executive Prakash Sikaria said agents generate 60-70% of its code and handle much of customer service.

Its consumer pilots include buying a wish-listed product when its price falls and purchasing gold under a systematic investment plan when prices dip. Sikaria called these "very early thoughts" and expected clarity within six months. Razorpay chief executive Harshil Mathur said Vulkan, its payments model trained on nearly four billion transactions, improved transaction success rates by 8-10% and checkout personalisation by up to 40%.

These applications optimise a customer-initiated payment rather than allowing AI to decide when or what to buy. Mathur said payment companies would need AI-led defences as attackers adopt AI. NPCI unveiled AiNxt for building agents and Agentic Orchestration and Messaging for UPI integration and certification. BharatPe said its assistant can work across more than 60 merchant systems, while L&T Finance and Pine Labs showcased flight-booking use cases.

Executives said such bounded deployments allow companies to test reliability before widening an agent's permissions. A year on, pilots remain narrow At GFF 2025, NPCI, Razorpay and OpenAI had demonstrated a Bigbasket purchase within ChatGPT, while Cashfree Payments unveiled a similar in-chat shopping-and-payment flow.

NPCI had also introduced UPI Help for transaction queries, mandate management and dispute resolution. NPCI said UPI Help is now available, but remains an assistance tool. Cashfree had announced redBus and Yatra integrations. The redBus flow requires customer approval at payment; the Yatra use case allows the agent to transact within conditions authorised in advance. Razorpay lists Agentic Payments as a product but did not disclose user or transaction data from its Bigbasket pilot at last year's GFF.

title: Fintechs High on AI, but Yet to let it Handle Your Money
